hints: Focus on the 1 to 1 to 1 to 1 mole ratio for acid + alcohol forming ester + water, so every mole of ester made uses up one mole of each reactant.
Since 0.20 mol of ester is made, 0.20 mol of water is also made, leaving 0.20 mol of acid and 0.10 mol of alcohol at equilibrium.
Put those four equilibrium amounts into Kc as products over reactants, remembering the volume cancels so you can use moles directly.
walkthrough:
**Write the balanced equation**

Think of esterification simply as one acid plus one alcohol making one ester plus one water. All the coefficients are 1, which makes the mole maths easy.

Chemical equation or calculation rule if applicable:
$$\text{acid} + \text{alcohol} \rightleftharpoons \text{ester} + \text{water}$$

**Find the equilibrium moles**

Start with 0.40 mol acid and 0.30 mol alcohol. Making 0.20 mol ester must use up 0.20 mol of each reactant and also make 0.20 mol of water.

Chemical equation or calculation rule if applicable:
$$n(\text{acid})_{eq} = 0.40 - 0.20 = 0.20 \text{ mol}$$
$$n(\text{alcohol})_{eq} = 0.30 - 0.20 = 0.10 \text{ mol}$$
$$n(\text{ester})_{eq} = n(\text{water})_{eq} = 0.20 \text{ mol}$$

**Write the Kc expression and calculate**

Kc uses equilibrium concentrations, products over reactants. Because there are two concentrations on top and two below, the volume V cancels, so we can just use equilibrium moles.

Chemical equation or calculation rule if applicable:
$$K_c = \frac{[\text{ester}][\text{water}]}{[\text{acid}][\text{alcohol}]} = \frac{(0.20/V)(0.20/V)}{(0.20/V)(0.10/V)}$$
$$K_c = \frac{0.20 \times 0.20}{0.20 \times 0.10} = \frac{0.040}{0.020} = 2.0$$

options.A: Incorrect. This uses the initial moles of acid and alcohol instead of the equilibrium moles. Kc must always use equilibrium values: (0.20 x 0.20)/(0.40 x 0.30) = 0.33, which ignores the 0.20 mol that reacted.
options.B: Incorrect. This is the upside down Kc, reactants over products. (0.20 x 0.10)/(0.20 x 0.20) = 0.50. Remember Kc for this reaction as written is products, ester and water, divided by reactants, acid and alcohol.
options.C: Correct. Well done. Equilibrium amounts are 0.20 mol acid, 0.10 mol alcohol, 0.20 mol ester and 0.20 mol water, so Kc = (0.20 x 0.20)/(0.20 x 0.10) = 2.0. It has no units here because the volumes cancel.
options.D: Incorrect. This forgets the water product and divides only by the reactants. 0.20/(0.20 x 0.10) = 10. Both products, ester and water, must be included in the numerator.
